ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 2 of 2011 (as amended by Law 15 of 2015, Executive Decree 37 of 2013, and the UAF Regulations); Law 1 of 2018 on Private Interest Foundations; Article 12 of Law 1 of 2018 regarding Foundation Council and Beneficial Owner filing through the registered agent; Resolution 016-2012 of the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) on customer due diligence; Cabinet Decree 363 of 2015 (AML/CFT regime for non-financial institutions) and the Public Registry of Panama directives on the declaration of beneficial owners (as codified under the Single Registry System for Ultimate Beneficial Owners, SIRUBO).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of execution or Panama Notary if executed locally

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent government authority

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, council members, protectors, beneficiaries, and disclosed UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK Sanctions List, and the Panamanian National Prompt Action Register (Registro de Personas Expuestas Políticamente PEP). Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family members, or close associates. Any positive hit or unresolved false positive requires written compliance sign-off and, for AML/CFT escalation, a suspicious transaction report to the UAF when financial activity is involved.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Plataforma de Servicios en Línea / Fundaciones y Personas Jurídicas (online name search and preliminary availability request via the Official Portal: www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names must be expressed in Latin script; if the desired name is not in Spanish, a Spanish transliteration format is generally required for registry processing. The name must not be identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered foundation, corporation, or branch. It must generally be followed by 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or an acceptable abbreviation (e.g., 'FIP') where the registry requires distinction. The use of the word 'Foundation' alone without appropriate Panamanian legal designation is not sufficient.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Public Registry rejects a name, the applicant or licensed registered agent may file a written reconsideration request within 3 business days using the official online administrative portal of the Public Registry, stating grounds of non-confusing distinction or acquiescence. If the rejection is maintained, a formal jurisdictional appeal may be filed with the Directora General del Registro Público within 5 business days of the second decision. The registry also permits a fresh name clearance filing with a modified version of the rejected name without penalty.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible for administrative correspondence and communications, but the foundation must maintain a physical registered office in Panama through a licensed registered agent (domiciliary agent). There is no statutory requirement to lease physical premises for the foundation's activities, provided the registered agent's street address in Panama serves as the registered address. For an electric cargo e-bike manufacturing business operating under a PIF, commercial substance would normally be evidenced by manufacturing contracts, bank accounts, decision-making records and beneficial operational control; a pure virtual office without underlying substance may be challenged for tax, banking, or economic substance review under international standards.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Private Interest Foundations Law of the Republic of Panama (Ley 25 de 12 de junio de 1995), as amended by Ley 13 de 2015; Articles 1-8, 13, 18 and 25 govern foundation formation, endowment, registration and the Foundation Council; supplementary application of Law 32 of 1927 for corporate governance gaps.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Publico de Panama) - Private Interest Foundations Section (Seccion de Fundaciones de Interes Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Foundation Charter (Escritura Publica de Constitucion de Fundacion de Interes Privado) filed and inscribed in the Private Interest Foundations Section
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. The Foundation Charter must express the initial endowment, which may be nominal or in kind; no escrow account or deposit certificate is required. Capital subscription is accepted at the first meeting of the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the capital subscription of the Founder in the Foundation's initial endowment is accepted and recorded in the Foundation's books; RESOLVED, that the registered office is fixed at the office of the Resident Agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama, as the legal domicile for all statutory purposes; RESOLVED, that the individuals named in the annexed schedule are appointed as initial members of the Foundation Council on two-year terms; RESOLVED, that the licensed Panamanian legal firm is appointed as Resident Agent; and RESOLVED, that the Chairman of the Foundation Council is instructed to execute all registry filings, pay all official fees, and take every act necessary to obtain the Foundation's inscription in the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Foundation's corporate name and obtain name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Foundations Section, online via the Sede Electronica service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the Registry's e-platform or at the Foundations Section window. The Registry performs an exact and phonetic search; if available, it issues a name-availability certificate and blocks the name for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of the Founder or Foundation Council member
Notarized power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the requested name is rejected for similarity or already registered, file a written reconsideration with alternate name options within five business days; the reservation fee for the rejected name is non-refundable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the Foundation Charter and Bylaws
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary of the Circuit of Panama; the charter must be notarized before presentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel drafts the Escritura Publica de Constitucion (Foundation Charter) and the Estatutos (Bylaws), specifying the Founder, initial endowment, lawful objects, Foundation Council composition, Resident Agent and registration clauses. The Founder signs the document before a public notary, and the notary issues certified copies.
required_dossiers: Declaracion de beneficiario final (beneficial ownership declaration)
Name-availability certificate from the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects drafting defects or conflicts with mandatory law, counsel amends the text and the document is re-executed; no registry record is affected until filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the notarial Foundation Charter with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Private Interest Foundations Section, Single Window (Ventanilla Unica de Fundaciones de Interes Privado), Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarial first copy, payment order and supporting documents to the Foundations Section. The Registry examines the legality of the objects, the endowment and the governing clauses. Upon approval, the foundation is inscribed and assigned a Folio Real number.
required_dossiers: Original certified notarial first copy of the Foundation Charter
Legalized copy of the Founder's constituent resolution if the Founder is a juridical person
Power of attorney of the Resident Agent
Proof of payment of the official registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice or reject notice, counsel files a legal corrective instrument (aclaratoria) or supplementary document within the prescribed cure period; failure to cure may result in refusal and loss of fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the registration certificate and open the statutory corporate books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama - Foundations Section; thereafter at the Foundation's registered office or through a licensed accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Collect the Certificado de Registro de Fundacion from the Registry. Appoint a local accountant and open the Minute Book, Resolutions Book and Accounting Ledger in accordance with Panamanian commercial record-keeping obligations; these books may remain private and need not be filed with the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the issued certificate contains data-entry errors, request a corrective certification from the Registry supported by the registered charter copy; the Registry will issue a rectified certificate within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for the tax identification number and complete the municipal operating patent formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Direccion General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; Municipality of Panama (Secretaria de Patentes y Licencias)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the DGI registration form to obtain the RUC (Registro Unico de Contribuyente) and, only if commercial or industrial activity is conducted from Panama, apply for the municipal patent or operating license. For a passive holding foundation, no municipal patent is required. The Resident Agent files the annual corporate tax obligations.
required_dossiers: Copy of registered office lease or notarized consent of the premises owner
Passport copies of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the municipality refuses processing, file a written reconsideration with corrected premises evidence within ten business days; late charges accrue only if economic activities commenced before the application date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) - Direccion General de Comercio Interior y Regulacion de Empresas, together with the Municipal Licensing Department of the local Alcaldia
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operacion and Licencia Comercial e Industrial (Commercial and Industrial Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) - Direccion de Verificacion del Desempeno Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II - Environmental Impact Assessment (EsIA) generally required for e-bike assembly and light manufacturing plants; Category I registration may suffice for low-complexity storage or assembly without battery formation, painting or electroplating; full EIA is triggered if battery cell manufacturing or hazardous chemical processes are included.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet the quality standards of Executive Decree No. 2 of 1982 and MiAMBIENTE implementing regulations; VOC and particulate emissions must comply with MiAMBIENTE air-emission limits and WHO health-based guidelines; lithium-ion battery waste must be handled, labeled, stored and transported under hazardous waste requirements, with approved treatment manifests.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification from the Benemerito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panama; municipal certificate of structural load inspection and building use; occupational health and workplace clearance from the Ministry of Health (MINSA) and the Directorate of Occupational Health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official electronic fiscal portal: 'Sede Electrónica' of the DGI — https://sede.mef.gob.pa (RUC registration, e-invoicing authorization, and ITBMS/ISR filings) complemented by https://dgi.mef.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF): (1) incorporate the foundation under Ley 25 de 1995 through a licensed foundation agent and record the public deed at the Registro Público de Panamá; (2) appoint a resident legal/fiscal representative with a Panama address and obtain the representative's Firma Electrónica (digital signature); (3) file the single RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application with the DGI, attaching the foundation deed, foundation reglamento, identification documents of founder and foundation council, appointment resolution, and proof of the Panamanian fiscal address; (4) DGI validates the ISIC 3091 economic-activity code (manufacture of electric cargo bicycles and scooters), assigns the permanent RUC, and activates ITBMS status if annual turnover equals or exceeds B/.300,000; (5) register the e-invoicing authorization in the same file. The standard processing window is 5-10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not maintain a US-style check-the-box regime or an OECD hybrid-mismatch election. Material statutory elections available to the PIF: (1) charter election under Ley 25 de 1995 (Art. 23) to exercise economic activities (manufacturing and trading) — once elected, the PIF becomes an ordinary ITBMS/ISR taxpayer on Panamanian-source activities while remaining territorial for foreign-source income; (2) simplified ITBMS regime election under Ley 8 de 2010 for taxpayers whose annual taxable turnover does not exceed B/.300,000; and (3) irrevocable reglamento election to classify distributions as tax-neutral foundation benefits payable to non-resident beneficiaries free of Panamanian withholding tax — the standard PIF structuring election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's VAT/GST-type tax on the transfer of goods and services, Código Fiscal Articles 1057-1080 and implementing rules of Ley 8 de 2010).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.300,000 (Panamanian Balboa, at 1:1 parity with the U.S. dollar) in taxable turnover during the preceding 12 months; taxpayers commencing activities must register prospectively when expected turnover will exceed the threshold, and may register voluntarily below it.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory certified electronic invoicing for every ITBMS taxpayer, including the PIF: (1) prior DGI authorization of the invoicing platform; (2) issuance of electronic invoices (machine-readable XML-equivalent format) carrying a unique DGI-validated 'constancia' (digital control token) and QR stamp — each invoice batch is transmitted to the DGI in near-real-time through the certified electronic-invoicing API/SOAP endpoints of the Sede Electrónica; (3) a specific electronic export invoice (factura de exportación) with zero-rate line, linked to the customs export declaration in the SISCOA/VUPE single window; and (4) retention of invoice transmissions and accounting books for at least five years. Invoices not transmitted to, or validated by, the DGI are null for input-credit purposes and trigger anti-evasion penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated export treatment under ITBMS (Código Fiscal Arts. 1061-1063; regulations of Ley 8 de 2010) applies to the PIF's electric cargo e-bike sales when: (a) the PIF is an active ITBMS taxpayer in good standing; (b) the goods are physically removed from Panamanian customs territory under a valid export declaration; (c) risk and title pass to a foreign buyer outside Panama under written Incoterms (FOB/CIF); and (d) the export proceeds are received through the Panamanian banking system in convertible foreign currency. Offshore and international services (transport, port, logistics, services consumed abroad) enjoy the same zero rate or are outside the tax. Zero-rating neutralizes output tax, preserving input-credit neutrality; an actual refund arises only when attributable input ITBMS on components exceeds zero-rated output. Panama's fully dollarized system imposes no statutory FX-repatriation deadline; the 180-day inward remittance benchmark is the customary evidentiary period for confirming export proceeds.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Formulario de Exportación) validated and exit-confirmed through the SISCOA/VUPE single-window system of the Panamanian customs authority
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure of the shipment from Panamanian customs territory
Zero-rated commercial export invoice bearing the DGI electronic-invoicing constancia/hash and the 0% ITBMS line
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by the collecting Panamanian bank for the export proceeds
Packing list and certificate of origin supporting the customs file (goods classified under HS 8711.60/8716; origin certificate where required by bilateral trade instruments)
Export sales contract and foundation board resolution establishing Incoterms, destination, foreign buyer identity, and the territorial-source evidence chain
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI export audits automatically cross-match zero-rated invoices against customs exit records (SISCOA) and banking-system inward remittance records. Any discrepancy reclassifies the transaction as a taxable domestic supply from the invoice date: the PIF owes the applicable ITBMS (currently 7%) plus 12% annual interest, a surcharge of 100% of the omitted tax, and fines of B/.1,000 to B/.50,000 under Código Fiscal Articles 765-768. Fraudulent zero-rating (invoice-only exports, re-importation after zero-rated export, falsified export declarations, or unpaid input claims) is aggravated tax fraud: criminal imprisonment of 2 to 5 years for the responsible foundation-council member or officer, nullity of invoices, revocation of the exporter registration and foundation commercial license, and joint and several civil liability of the foundation council to the DGI and the Empresa Nacional de Aduanas.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no traditional central bank. The Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent, while the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) exercises prudential regulation and supervision over banking institutions under Decree Law 2 of 2008. The Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) administers fiscal policy. No foreign exchange administration authority exists because the US Dollar is legal tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates a fully dollarized economy: the US Dollar is legal tender for all transactions, and the Panamanian Balboa exists solely as a fractional coin unit pegged 1:1 to the USD. Both current account and capital account transactions are fully and freely convertible, with zero exchange controls and no surrender or conversion obligations. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, capital repatriation, and trade settlements face no statutory hurdles, prior authorization, foreign investment screening, or withholding consent thresholds. The only practical friction is bank-level compliance (AML/KYC and FATF-related enhanced due diligence, given Panama's historical grey-listing), which does not restrict convertibility itself.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no surrender requirement for export receipts in USD or foreign currency. Exporters may freely hold, transact, or repatriate proceeds through local or offshore bank accounts without central-bank reporting or licensing. The only administrative duty is compliance with anti-money-laundering recordkeeping and beneficial-ownership declaration under Law 23 of 2015 and Law 254 of 2021.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (multi-currency USD/EUR receivables and trade disbursements)
Operational Account (fiscal-agent bank; low appetite for non-resident PIFs)
Operational Account plus Trade Finance (LC issuance and negotiation)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BAC International Bank, Inc. (BAC Credomatic Panama)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with international wire and merchant capacity

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium. Panama does not license a dedicated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) category; non-bank payment entities operate only as licensed 'empresas de remesas' (money remittance businesses) under SBP Circular rules and cannot open full transactional accounts or issue clearing-capable IBANs in USD domestically. Offshore EMIs (e.g., UK FCA, Lithuanian ECB passported, or class-3 EMI licenses) generally reject Panama-domiciled Private Interest Foundations as high-risk clients, and any virtual USD IBAN they issue lacks direct access to Panama's local ACH/SWIFT clearing. A compliant strategy is to pair a local Panamanian bank account as the primary clearing anchor with an offshore EMI solely for European corridors (EUR), provided the EMI accepts Panama country risk; otherwise, use traditional correspondent banking via tier-1 local banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch interview is effectively mandatory for a non-resident Private Interest Foundation at the account-opener (council member or duly authorized foundation officer) for most tier-1 banks. Remote onboarding is formally allowed under SBP's non-face-to-face KYC rules but is rarely approved for PIFs due to their hybrid legal character; in practice, at least one natural person signing on the account must appear in person with original passport, apostilled foundation deed, and council resolutions. Banks with established international desks (Banistmo, BAC, Multibank) may accept a two-step process: video verification with apostilled notarized documents, followed by a couriered certified copy and a physical visit at a regional office within 90 days; however, strict SBP-supervised institutions will not waive the initial physical meeting for a Panama-domiciled PIF.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal entity type flag: Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is perceived as a low-transparency hybrid vehicle frequently used for asset protection, triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled Foundation Charter and initial nomination deed; valid Private Interest Foundation certificate issued by the Public Registry of Panama; final beneficial owner declaration submitted to the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales under Law 254 of 2021; audited or certified source-of-funds statement; a written business-purpose memo confirming active industrial manufacturing of electric cargo e-bikes under ISIC 3091, not passive wealth holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident control and nominee council membership creating a shadow-direction (yellow-flag) profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full disclosure of the council members and protector (if any); sworn declaration of the economic group structure; identification of the ultimate controller with passport and proof of tax residence; management services agreement; bank reference letters from the controller's home-country bank; organigram showing the operational role of the Panamanian entity in the trade chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Country-risk and reputational flag: Panama's prior FATF grey-listing (removed after progress, still closely watched) and EU/OECD tax-list mentions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent FATF compliance status confirmation; Panama Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) and multilateral conventions; certified copy of the entity's Panama VAT and income-tax registrations; evidence of filing obligations under the non-resident-business framework; U.S. OFAC and sanctions checklist signed by the client; a detailed trade-contract trail with independent counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected transaction pattern mismatch: high-value inbound capital injections and outbound trade payments hitting a newly opened account without prior relationship history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Pro-forma invoices and signed purchase orders for battery packs, motors, and aluminum frames; full bill-of-lading and customs-import evidence; lease agreement for the manufacturing/warranty facility; payroll or manufacturing subcontractor contracts; 12-month cash-flow forecast; signed representation letter confirming no cash-intensive or high-value-goods proceeds without documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Convertibility and protocol ambiguity: bank queries on the legal basis for USD positions in a country without FX controls, and potential confusion with other Latin American currency regulations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Panama Monetary Regime legal opinion citing Law 84 of 1904 and the non-existence of exchange-control statutes; a legal memorandum from a Panamanian counsel confirming USD legal tender status and absence of surrender obligations; a standard compliance attestation that all funds will be cleared in USD with no need for central-bank filings.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections (equity contribution, shareholder loan, or working-capital advance from the ultimate controlling shareholder) must be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the funding bank to the PIF's USD account at the Panamanian bank. The wire must clearly specify: (a) in field 50K, the ordering party's full legal name and account number (matching the entity's UBO declaration); (b) in field 59, the beneficiary as the exact PIF legal name per foundation deed; (c) in field 70 (Remittance Information), a precise purpose narrative such as 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION FOR MANUFACTURING WORKING CAPITAL – ISIC 3091' or 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN FOR TRADE DISBURSEMENTS – ELEC CARGO EBIKE' plus the referenced loan agreement number. The mandatory documentation bundle: signed board/council resolution authorizing the account opening and the specific wire; copy of the foundation deed and UBO registry certificate (apostilled); source-of-wealth and source-of-funds affidavits; loan agreement (if loan, with interest rate and term); and the latest financial statements of the transferring entity if the amount exceeds USD 250,000. Panama requires no central-bank approval or purpose-code filing, but the receiving bank will apply SBP's enhanced due diligence, and the outbound credit advice must be retained as part of the AML file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements for component procurement (typical suppliers in China and the EU) should be cleared through: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct telegraphic-transfer payments under USD 100,000 per invoice, with field 70 describing the invoice number and Incoterms; (2) SWIFT MT700 / MT710 for documentary Letters of Credit for larger or recurring supply contracts, allowing sight drafts against presented B/L, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, and quality certificates; (3) SWIFT MT799 / MT760 for standby LCs or guarantees supporting pre-shipment deposits. All disbursements must reference the underlying purchase contract, utilize standard 3-digit currency codes (USD, EUR, CNY when permitted), and maintain at least 2-of-3 signature authorization by the foundation council to satisfy banking control requirements. Payment confirmation and reconciliation must reconcile automatically to the ERP in real time, with original documents archived for the mandatory five-year AML retention period.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX Forwards (USD/EUR, USD/CNY, USD/GBP) with non-Panamanian international counterparties or local bank treasury desks; no regulatory restriction since Panama has no exchange controls, but only account-holder level credit-approval constraints.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., USD/CNY NDF, USD/COP NDF, USD/MXN NDF) to hedge component sourcing and Latin-American sales exposures without physical settlement in non-tradeable currencies.

Cross-Currency Swaps (USD/EUR and USD/CNY) for asset-liability alignment on medium-term supply or distribution contracts, transacted under ISDA 2002 master agreements with authorized international dealers.

FX Swap (liquidity-swap) Transactions fiat-to-fiat, and dynamic rolling of forward positions, permissible without central-bank authorization but subject to bank-specific derivative licensing and board-approved financial-risk delegation.

At-the-Money or Vanilla Currency Options (buy-side only) for EUR and CNY exposures where the foundation does not hold speculative positions; options must be economically hedged and documented via a treasury policy.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat Panama-source corporate income tax (ISR) for S.A.s, corporations and Private Interest Foundations (PIFs) deriving Panamanian-source income; Panama applies a territorial system, so income from genuinely foreign sources is excluded from the taxable base. The 5-year loss carryforward exists but no carryback is permitted.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sectoral holiday applies to ISIC 3091 under the general regime. Structural advantages: (i) territorial exclusion of foreign-source revenue; (ii) dividends received by a PIF shareholder from a Panamanian operating subsidiary are not re-taxed after the final dividend WHT is imposed at the distributing level; (iii) qualifying export-manufacturing plants located in an EPZ or SEM regime (e.g. Panama Pacifico, Colon Free Zone) may access a 0%-10% CIT rate and dividend WHT exemptions; (iv) accelerated depreciation and R&D deductions for e-mobility tooling and battery-testing equipment may be claimed under specific DGI rulings.
